args.text: The bug is on line 31-34: `ssl.SSLError` is caught but immediately re-raised as `RelayTlsError` instead of retrying. The fix is to let `ssl.SSLError` fall through the loop like any other transient error.
Now let me verify the tests pass:

All 3 tests pass. The fix: `ssl.SSLError` is now caught and treated as a transient fault (sets `last`, continues the loop) instead of immediately aborting. After `retries` exhaustion it raises `TlsError` (or `RelayTlsError`, both are acceptable since the latter subclasses the former). The `self.context` passed to every attempt always originates from `build_context()` which uses `ssl.create_default_context()` — full certificate verification is preserved.

Done. The `ssl.SSLError` handler on line 31-33 now records the error in `last` and `continue`s the retry loop instead of immediately raising. Certificate verification (`check_hostname=True`, `verify_mode=CERT_REQUIRED`) is unchanged — the same `self.context` from `build_context()` is passed on every attempt.
